---
title: "Flag differences in NRT"
format:
  html:
    page-layout: full
execute:
  echo: false
---

What is left after the two previous pages: profiles at sea, marked NRT, and
not estimated to carry delayed mode flags. The estimate is made per
variable, so each variable is counted over its own profiles: one whose
salinity looks reworked by an operator is in the temperature figures and
not in the salinity ones. Both flags on them should come
from automated tests, so where they disagree, the tests differ. Either one
side runs a test the other does not, or both run it with different logic or
thresholds.

The two sides of a disagreement can be read to different depths. nrtqclib
records which of its checks failed, so an observation only nrtqclib flags
can be traced to the check, or checks, behind it. The input carries one
flag per variable and nothing about how it was reached, so an observation
only the input flags is described by where it is and which value the input
gave it.

```{ojs}
//| output: false
app = import(new URL("assets/js/app.js", document.baseURI).href)
meta = app.loadAnalyses()
name = (id) => app.datasetName(meta, id)
table = app.analysisTable
byDataset = (a, b) => app.datasetOrder(meta, a.dataset_id) - app.datasetOrder(meta, b.dataset_id)
variableLabel = (n) => meta.variables.find((v) => v.name === n)?.label ?? n
statusLabel = (k) => meta.statuses.find((s) => s.key === k)?.label ?? k
status = meta ? app.loadAnalysisTable("items_status") : null
totals = new Map((status ?? []).reduce((m, r) => {
  const key = `${r.dataset_id}|${r.variable}`;
  m.set(key, (m.get(key) ?? 0) + r.n_obs);
  return m;
}, new Map()))
```

```{ojs}
meta === null ? app.analysesMissing() : html``
```

## How often they disagree

```{ojs}
meta ? app.analysisFigure(
  "items_status",
  "Observations flagged by both sources, by the input alone and by nrtqclib alone, per 1,000 observations of NRT profiles at sea.",
  "Bars of the three flagged categories per product and variable."
) : html``
```

```{ojs}
statusRows = status
  ? app.widen(status, { index: ["dataset_id", "variable"], column: "status", value: "n_obs" })
      .sort((a, b) => byDataset(a, b) || a.variable.localeCompare(b.variable) * -1)
  : []
meta ? table(statusRows, [
  { key: "dataset_id", label: "Product", align: "left", format: name },
  { key: "variable", label: "Variable", align: "left", format: variableLabel },
  { key: "total", label: "Observations", format: (_, r) => app.formatCount(totals.get(`${r.dataset_id}|${r.variable}`)) },
  ...meta.statuses.map((s) => ({
    key: s.key, label: `${s.label} per 1,000`,
    format: (v, r) => app.formatRate(app.perThousandOf(v, totals.get(`${r.dataset_id}|${r.variable}`)))
  }))
]) : html``
```

## Which nrtqclib checks account for what only nrtqclib flags

An observation can fail more than one check. The dark part of a bar is the
observations this check alone flagged, which nothing else in nrtqclib would
have caught; the light part is those it flagged together with other checks.

```{ojs}
meta ? app.analysisFigure(
  "items_attribution",
  "Observations only nrtqclib flags, per 1,000 observations, by the check that failed. Checks that never contributed are left out. Note the different scales across products.",
  "Bar charts per product and variable of nrtqclib-only observations by check."
) : html``
```

```{ojs}
byItem = meta ? app.loadAnalysisTable("items_by_item") : null
viewof itemDataset = meta && byItem
  ? Inputs.select([...new Set(byItem.map((r) => r.dataset_id))], { label: "Product", format: name })
  : html``
```

```{ojs}
meta && byItem ? table(
  byItem.filter((r) => r.dataset_id === itemDataset && r.n_fail > 0),
  [
    { key: "variable", label: "Variable", align: "left", format: variableLabel },
    { key: "item", label: "Check", align: "left", format: (_, r) => app.qcCheck(r.column, meta.variables).label },
    { key: "column", label: "Column", align: "left", format: (v) => v },
    { key: "n_fail", label: "Failed" },
    { key: "n_fail_agree_bad", label: "Also flagged by the input" },
    { key: "n_fail_nrtqclib_only", label: "Only nrtqclib" },
    { key: "n_alone_nrtqclib_only", label: "This check alone" }
  ]
) : html``
```

The commonest sets of failing checks behind the observations only nrtqclib
flags, over every NRT product together. A column is one set; the dots below
it say which checks are in it.

```{ojs}
meta ? app.analysisFigure(
  "items_combinations",
  "The ten commonest sets of failing nrtqclib checks among observations only nrtqclib flags, pooled over the NRT products.",
  "UpSet charts, one per variable, of check combinations."
) : html``
```

## Where in the water column

```{ojs}
meta ? app.analysisFigure(
  "items_depth",
  "Observations flagged by one source alone, per 1,000 observations in each pressure band. Colour is the product and line type the region.",
  "Line charts of disagreement rates against pressure, per variable and source."
) : html``
```

## What the input called the values only it flags

The input flag of each observation it flags and nrtqclib does not. A value
the input calls probably bad (3) is a softer disagreement than one it calls
bad (4).

```{ojs}
flagsTable = meta ? app.loadAnalysisTable("items_original_flags") : null
originalOnly = flagsTable
  ? app.widen(
      flagsTable.filter((r) => r.nrtqclib_bad === false &&
        (meta.variables.find((v) => v.name === r.variable)?.bad_flag_values ?? []).includes(r.original_flag)),
      { index: ["dataset_id", "variable"], column: "original_flag", value: "n_obs", name: (v) => `f${v}` }
    ).sort((a, b) => byDataset(a, b) || a.variable.localeCompare(b.variable) * -1)
  : []
flagKeys = [...new Set(originalOnly.flatMap((r) => Object.keys(r).filter((k) => /^f\d+$/.test(k))))].sort()
meta ? table(originalOnly, [
  { key: "dataset_id", label: "Product", align: "left", format: name },
  { key: "variable", label: "Variable", align: "left", format: variableLabel },
  ...flagKeys.map((k) => ({ key: k, label: app.flagWithMeaning(Number(k.slice(1))) }))
]) : html``
```

## By platform

The platforms of one product, with their rates of each kind of
disagreement. Sort by a column to find the platforms a disagreement comes
from; the [Platforms](platforms.qmd) page opens their profiles.

```{ojs}
platforms = meta ? app.loadAnalysisTable("items_platforms") : null
viewof platformDataset = meta && platforms
  ? Inputs.select([...new Set(platforms.map((r) => r.dataset_id))], { label: "Product", format: name })
  : html``
```

```{ojs}
// One row per platform, each variable's counts over its own NRT profiles.
platformRows = platforms
  ? [...platforms
      .filter((r) => r.dataset_id === platformDataset)
      .reduce((m, r) => {
        const row = m.get(r.platform_code) ?? { key: r.platform_code, platform_code: r.platform_code };
        row[`${r.variable}_profiles`] = r.n_profiles;
        row[`${r.variable}_obs`] = r.n_obs;
        row[`${r.variable}_oo`] = app.perThousandOf(r.n_original_only, r.n_obs);
        row[`${r.variable}_no`] = app.perThousandOf(r.n_nrtqclib_only, r.n_obs);
        m.set(r.platform_code, row);
        return m;
      }, new Map()).values()]
  : []
meta && platforms ? table(
  platformRows,
  [
    { key: "platform_code", label: "Platform", align: "left", format: (v) => v },
    ...meta.variables.flatMap((v) => [
      { key: `${v.name}_profiles`, label: `${v.label}: profiles`, format: (x) => (x == null ? "" : app.formatCount(x)) },
      { key: `${v.name}_oo`, label: `original only per 1,000`, format: app.formatRate },
      { key: `${v.name}_no`, label: `nrtqclib only per 1,000`, format: app.formatRate }
    ])
  ],
  { sortKey: `${meta.variables[0].name}_profiles`, descending: true }
) : html``
```
